tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

pulsed-single-qubit-params: Section III-A, p.5-6, Eq. 7: four parameters per single-qubit pulse, duration and shape fixed; states no expressivity gain.
pulsed-two-qubit-params: Section III-B, p.6-7: single CR-inspired pulse with amplitude, phase and detuning as the three learnable parameters.
pulsed-pulse-shape: Section IV-A, p.7: sinusoidal constant-amplitude control field; rotation angle linear in Omega T.
pulsed-warm-start: Section II-B, p.3-4 and Fig. 3: first-qubit parameters copied, second random, two-qubit parameters zero; the cost depends only on the first qubit, so initial cost equals the single-qubit final cost.
pulsed-loss-targets: Section IV-A, p.7, Eqs. 8-10: fidelity loss from [13], general single-qubit target states with learnable theta and phi.
pulsed-datasets-splits: Section IV-A, p.7: MNIST 0 vs 8 with PCA to 3 dims, Iris versicolor vs virginica, Corners, Helix; 300/100 and 70/30 splits as stated.
pulsed-simulation-method: Section IV-A p.8: custom pennylane extension; note 58 (references, p.16): Trotter-Suzuki, each pulse divided into dozens of gates.
pulsed-noise-model: Appendix B.3, p.12-13: channels after each pulse or single-qubit gate, SPAM flips, ECR error for two-qubit depolarizing, X and sqrt-X errors averaged for single-qubit.
pulsed-device-params: Table I caption, p.7: Brisbane qubit 1 and 2 statistics taken from the public device datasheet [54].
pulsed-noise-sweep-setup: Section IV-C, p.9: 20 layers, Table I noise fixed, depolarizing p from 0 to 0.3.
pulsed-scaling-open: Section V, p.11: authors state simulation cost limits the work to two qubits and larger registers need new simulation infrastructure.
pulsed-encoding-confound: Section V, p.11: second stated limitation, the encoding stage stays gate-based; pulse-level encoding would add confounders needing a dedicated study.
pulsed-noise-range: Section IV-C, p.10: authors state the explored depolarizing probabilities exceed typical single-gate error rates and call the sweep a stress test.
pulsed-sim-setup: Section I p.2 and IV-A p.8: Brisbane-derived noise, four tasks, two-qubit only, five seeds; all are the paper's own setup statements.
pulsed-stated-limits: Section V, p.11: 'We acknowledge two main limitations', two-qubit simulations only and gate-based encoding.
cql-definition: Abstract, p.1, and Introduction p.2: CQL defined as parameters promoted to quantum degrees of freedom evolved under a loss Hamiltonian.
cql-scope-learning: Introduction, p.2: authors state CQL is designed specifically for learning problems with a model-on-data objective.
cql-discretization: CQL protocol, p.2: m-bit discretization, 2^m grid in [0,2pi), basis state on m ancillas.
cql-hamiltonian-form: CQL protocol, Eq. 1, p.2: Hamiltonian with kinetic Laplacian term and diagonal loss term with damping functions, built on QHD [28].
cql-initial-state: CQL protocol, p.2: uniform superposition without prior information, Gaussian wavepacket with an informed guess.
cql-clock-register: CQL protocol, p.2 and Supplement I, p.10: clock register turns time dependence into a position operator, giving Eq. 2, at the cost of a larger space.
cql-block-encoding-assumed: CQL protocol, p.2: complexity moves to simulating Eq. 2 and block-encoding access is assumed throughout.
cql-classifier-model: CQL protocol, Eqs. 3-4, p.3: reduced data re-uploading model with Ry trainable rotation and loss 1 - |alpha_y|^2.
cql-coherent-evaluation: CQL protocol, Eq. 5, p.3: unitary U_x,theta evaluates the model over all grid values, entangling outputs with parameters.
cql-batch-per-ancilla: CQL protocol, p.3 and Supplement I.C.1, p.13: one output qubit per data point for a coherent batch.
cql-operator-discretization-scope: CQL protocol, p.3: authors state non-unique discretization and that optimal discretization and norm control are beyond the scope.
cql-batched-protocol: Batched CQL, p.3-4: dataset partitioned into batches processed sequentially, each final state starting the next evolution.
cql-global-batch-impractical: Batched CQL, p.3: authors state a whole-dataset batch needs one ancilla per data point and is not realistic.
cql-algorithm-batched: Supplement II, Algorithm 1, p.16: per batch build loss Hamiltonian, evolve for tau, pass the state on with no classical measurement.
cql-joint-batch-loss: Supplement I.C.1, p.13: joint loss I minus the product of correct-classification probabilities is derived for two samples, and the authors state it is a product-type objective, not the empirical mean loss.
cql-classif-setup-appendix: Supplement III, p.17: five qubits per parameter, grid over (-pi, pi), 2pi/2^5 about 0.20 rad, inside-or-outside interval task with noise, 100 train and 500 test samples.
cql-classif-schedule-baseline: Supplement III, p.17: total time 10^-2 chosen heuristically, uniform initial state, SGD baseline with learning rate 0.1.
cql-mzi-setup: Numerical demonstrations (b), p.5: balanced MZI with unknown phase phi and controllable theta; loss sin^2((theta-phi)/2) minimal at theta = phi.
cql-mzi-simulated: Numerical demonstrations (b), p.5 and Supplement IV.B, p.18: coherent simulation, target state set in the simulator.
cql-mzi-numerics-params: Supplement IV.B, p.18: n=5 (32 points), T=5.0 with 1000 slices (dt 5e-3), damping 1/t and t.
cql-mzi-loss-appendix: Supplement IV.B, p.18: loss landscape defined as 1 - |<psi_target|psi(theta)>|^2 in the simulator.
cql-open-directions: Conclusion, p.6: authors list complexity analyses, better Hamiltonian constructions and discretizations, and error mitigation as open.
cql-code-availability: Code and data availability, p.6: repository nacedob/Coherent-Quantum-Learning named by the authors.
cql-complexity-open: Numerical demonstrations (a), p.4-5: full complexity analysis beyond scope; asymptotic advantage over hybrid optimization stated as an open question.
cql-demo-setup: Numerical demonstrations (a), p.4-5: single-qubit re-uploading circuit, two layers, two parameters, five qubits each, one epoch in the single-sample regime.
hybrid-model-three-elements: Abstract, p.1: the authors' own model description with three elements.
architecture-pqrnn-cb-ansatz: Sections 2.1-2.2, p.3-4: pQRNN with CB ansatz chosen, following [14].
encoding-rotation-arccos: Section 2.1, p.3: x-axis rotation with arccos of the normalized input, replicated over Register D qubits.
prediction-definition-first-qubit-probab: Section 2.1, p.4: probability of the first Register D qubit collapsing to |1> after a Z measurement is the prediction.
qubo-definition-binary-variables: Section 3, p.5, Eq. 3: QUBO form with binary variables, linear and quadratic coefficients.
task-stock-trend-prediction: Section 4.1, p.5: the problem is the increase or decrease of the next closing price.
training-record-format: Section 4.1, p.5, Table 1: records hold x(t), x(t-1) and a 1/0 closing indicator.
classical-training-spsa: Section 4.3, p.6: classical training by gradient descent with the SPSA optimizer.
objective-functions-classical-and-adiaba: Section 4.3 Eq. 4, p.6 (log(p+e^-10) averaged over N) and Section 4.4, p.7 (MSE for adiabatic training); the text layer drops the sign and summation.
accuracy-metric-hit-counts: Section 4.3, p.6: average regression accuracy (hit counts) evaluates the model.
state-vector-encoding-example: Section 4.4, Eqs. 5-6, p.7: worked example of the paper's own encoding; vector entries match the quotes and cos/sin of the encoded angle.
ansatz-operator-diagonal-16x16: Section 4.4, p.7: ansatz operator given as a 16x16 diagonal matrix.
phase-factor-omitted-real-values-only: Section 4.5, p.8: phase factor i omitted because state vectors are real and QUBO needs real values.
discretization-loses-precision: Section 4.5, p.8: authors state angle discretization loses precision.
discretization-four-parts-angle-values: Section 5, p.9, Table 3: discretization in 4 parts with the listed angle values.
results-from-typical-execution: Section 5, p.8-9: authors state the reported results are from a typical execution.
compute-setup-local-pc: Section 5, p.9: local PC, python framework, 32,602 MB memory.
dataset-yahoo-finance-split: Section 5, p.9: Yahoo Finance data, 80/20 train/test split.
execution-count-definition: Section 6, p.10: EC defined per method.
annealing-simulator-no-step-access: Section 6, p.10: simulator gives no access to internal evolution steps.
barren-plateau-comparison-future-work: Section 7, p.11: Barren Plateau comparison left to future research.
future-work-overcome-expressiveness-loss: Section 7, p.11: alternatives to overcome the expressiveness loss recommended as future work.
future-work-more-diverse-datasets-scalab: Section 7, p.11: more diverse datasets needed to verify scalability and robustness.
adiabatic-training-expressiveness-limit: Section 7, p.11: authors state QUBO binary nature reduces expressiveness through angle discretization; consistent with Section 4.5.
adiabatic-training-scope-simulated-only: Section 5, p.9: Qiskit and D-Wave Ocean simulation; real noisy hardware left to further research.
five-benchmark-attribute-definitions: Section 2.1, p.4-5: the five attributes are defined in the paper's own list.
attributes-not-strict-definitions: Section 2.1, p.4: attributes not strict definitions, allow flexibility.
five-metric-properties: Section 2.3, p.8: practical, repeatable, reliable, linear, consistent as listed; polynomial-time gloss stated for practical.
scope-quantum-processors-only: Section 2, p.3: 'we will restrict ourselves to the evaluation of the performance of quantum processors'; focus on measurement of actual systems.
table1-binary-assessment-method: Section 3.4.2, p.18-19: only satisfied or not is recorded; causes of failure named.
table1-valid-for-nisq-only: Section 3.4.3, p.26: evaluations hold for the NISQ era, not post-NISQ.
speqc-mock-report-illustrative-only: Section 4.3, p.35: Fig. 5 is an example of a possible report.
benchmark-attributes-hard-together: Conclusion, p.35: authors state meeting all attributes at once can be challenging.
benchmark-guidelines-aim: Abstract, p.1: authors propose general guidelines aimed at a roadmap to standardization; Section 4 gives them.
convergence-criteria-definition: Section VI.A, p.9: two stated criteria (mean return in [mu-sigma, mu], at most 1% failures in last 1000), both before 5000 episodes.
statistics-10-runs: Section VI.A, p.9: plots average 20 episodes over 10 runs, shading is one standard deviation.
fair-comparison-parameter-matched: Section VI.A, p.9: each configuration compared to a classical SAC of equal learnable-parameter count, same hyperparameters, optimizer and activations where possible.
environment-two-link-250-steps: Section IV.A, p.5-6: Box2D two-link arm adapted from Gym Acrobot-v1, 250 steps, reward -d or +5.
vqc-architecture-hybrid-actor: Section V.B, p.9: angle encoding, data re-uploading, Pauli-Z measurement, VQC replaces the input layer.
noise-not-studied-limit: Section VI.A, p.9: noise not explored because of simulation nature and long training time.
future-work-hardware-needed: Section VII, p.12: physical quantum computer evaluation future work; real-device behavior with noise unknown.
acuto-setup-digital-simulation: Abstract p.1 and Section VI.A p.9: digital simulation with TensorFlow Quantum on Cirq; noise not explored. The widened value matches the passages.

theory_low.cql-loss-block-encoding: p.3 and Supplement I.C, p.12: the (1, m+5, 0) parameters follow from Theorem 2 of Rattew and Rebentrost [46] and the product rule from [47]; both are cited, not proved here. Not a result proved in this paper.
theory_low.cql-periodic-grid-momentum: Supplement I.B, p.11-12: an illustration of a block encoding 'without mitigating the scaling'; the t ~ delta-x scaling, called exponential in qubits, is asserted, not derived or proved.
